nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain. Then $A$ is integrally closed and has Krull dimension at most one if and only if $A$ is a Dedekind domain.
nodes.title: Dedekind domains are the integrally closed Noetherian domains of dimension at most one

nodes.summary: An integral domain $A$ is a Dedekind domain if and only if $A$ is Noetherian and, for all ideals $I$ and $J$ of $A$, $I$ divides $J$ if and only if $J \subseteq I$.
nodes.title: Dedekind domains as the Noetherian domains where to contain is to divide

nodes.summary: An integral domain $A$ is a Dedekind domain if and only if for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ there is an ideal $J$ of $A$ such that $IJ$ is a nonzero principal ideal.
nodes.title: Dedekind domains via principal products

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain such that for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ and every nonzero $a \in I$ there is $b \in A$ with $I = (a, b)$. Then $A$ is a Dedekind domain.
nodes.title: Dedekind domains from two generators with one prescribed

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain such that for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ the quotient ring $A/I$ is a principal ideal ring. Then $A$ is a Dedekind domain.
nodes.title: Dedekind domains from principal quotients

nodes.summary: For an integral domain $A$, the following are equivalent: (1) $A$ is a Dedekind domain; (2) $A$ is Noetherian and, for all ideals $I$ and $J$ of $A$, $I$ divides $J$ if and only if $J \subseteq I$; (3) for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ there is an ideal $J$ of $A$ such that $IJ$ is a nonzero principal ideal.
nodes.title: Equivalent characterizations of Dedekind domains

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain such that for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ the quotient ring $A/I$ is a principal ideal ring. Then for every nonzero prime ideal $P$ of $A$, the localization $A_P$ is a discrete valuation ring.
nodes.title: Principal quotients give discrete valuation rings at nonzero primes

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain. Then the localizations $A_P$ at all nonzero prime ideals $P$ of $A$ are discrete valuation rings if and only if $A$ is integrally closed and has Krull dimension at most one.
nodes.title: DVR localizations in a Noetherian domain

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain such that for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ the quotient ring $A/I$ is a principal ideal ring. Then $A$ is a Noetherian ring.
nodes.title: Domains with principal quotients are Noetherian

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain such that for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ and every nonzero $a \in I$ there is $b \in A$ with $I = (a, b)$. Then for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$, the quotient ring $A/I$ is a principal ideal ring.
nodes.title: Two generators with one prescribed give principal quotients

nodes.summary: Every quotient of a Dedekind domain by a nonzero ideal is a principal ideal ring.
nodes.title: Quotients of Dedekind domains by nonzero ideals are principal ideal rings

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
